executiveSummary: Senior Full Stack Software Engineer with 14+ years architecting scalable systems across web, cloud, and AI/ML domains. Currently modernizing aerospace manufacturing at Northrop Grumman while implementing ML automation and RAG systems. Proven technical leader who consistently delivers practical solutions that ship – from migrating 500+ microservices to optimizing legacy systems for 10x performance.
personal.valueProposition: I'm a senior full stack engineer who ships production code that scales. After 14+ years building everything from React frontends to distributed microservices, I've deliberately moved into AI/ML implementation because that's where the highest-leverage problems are. Currently at Northrop Grumman, I'm not just theorizing about AI – I'm building RAG systems, implementing predictive maintenance, and automating critical aerospace manufacturing processes. My superpower is taking complex technical problems and delivering practical solutions that actually work in production. Whether it's architecting 500+ microservices at AmeriSave or migrating 20-year-old VB6 systems, I measure success by business impact, and my strength is applying 14 years of systems architecture experience to make AI/ML solutions work reliably in production.

principles: Start with the business problem, not the technology
approach: Understand constraints first: Budget, timeline, team skills, existing systems
Design for the next 18 months: Not 10 years – requirements will change
Document trade-offs explicitly: Every decision has pros and cons
Build in observability from day one: You can't optimize what you can't measure
Plan for failure: Systems fail; good architectures handle it gracefully

faqs.leaving_role: The Northrop contract is going well, but I want to work on more modern tech stacks and specifically transition into AI/ML engineering. Plus, I'd love to relocate to Fort Collins or one of my other target cities. Dallas is fine, but I miss the mountains.
faqs.ai_experience: I've been implementing ML solutions in production for the past 2 years – predictive maintenance, computer vision, RAG systems, and LLM applications. I'm not an ML researcher, but I excel at taking ML models and making them work reliably at scale. My 14 years of systems experience means I know how to handle the infrastructure, monitoring, and edge cases that make ML actually useful in production.
faqs.not_bored: Not at all. I genuinely enjoy solving problems and shipping code. Some of my best work has been 'boring' – like optimizing database queries or refactoring legacy code. I find satisfaction in making things work better, regardless of how cutting-edge the technology is.
faqs.location_preferences: Quality of life. Fort Collins has great outdoor access and a tech scene. Santa Fe is beautiful with a smaller but growing tech community. Austin has energy and opportunities. Seattle... well, it's a tech hub. I've done my time in Dallas traffic and I'm ready for a change.
faqs.leave_defense: Yes. While the work is important and stable, I want to work on products that I can talk about at meetups, contribute to open source, and iterate quickly without multi-month approval processes. I miss the energy of commercial software development.
